'''Ihor Rafailovych Yukhnovskyi''' ({{langx|uk|Iгор Рафаïлович Юхновський}}; also '''Yukhnovsky'''; 1 September 1925 – 26 March 2024) was a Ukrainian physicist and politician,<ref name="Verkhovna Rada">{{cite web | url=http://gska2.rada.gov.ua:7777/site/dep_eng/Yukhnovskyi_I.HTM | title=Member of Parliament: Ihor Yukhnovskyi | accessdate=15 February 2011 | date=21 August 2006 | publisher= [[Verkhovna Rada|Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine]] }}{{Dead link|date=January 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> and a member of the Presidium of [[Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]], [[Hero of Ukraine]].

==Life before politics==
Yukhnovskyi was born on 1 September 1925, in Kniahynyne village, Dubno powiat, [[Wołyń Voivodeship (1921–1939)|Wołyń Voivodeship]] ([[Second Polish Republic|Poland]]). In 1944–1945 he participated in [[World War II]] on the side of [[Red Army]]. In 1951 he became the head of [[Theoretical Physics]] Department at [[Lviv University]]. In 1969 Yukhnovskyi, at that time Doctor of Physics and Mathematics led the newly organized Department of Statistical Theory of Condensed Matter. In 1980 the department was reorganized into the Lviv division of statistical physics for the [[Lviv Institute for Theoretical Physics|Institute for Theoretical Physics]], and then in 1990 into the Institute of [[Condensed Matter Physics]] of the [[National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]].<ref name=USUBC>{{cite web | url=http://www.usubc.org/AUR/aur706.php#a17 | accessdate=15 February 2011 | title=PRESIDENT YUSHCHENKO APPOINTS YUKHNOVSKYI DIRECTOR OF UKRAINE'S INSTITUTE OF NATIONAL REMEMBRANCE | date=22 May 2006 | publisher=US-Ukraine Business Council, republishing from the [[Ukrainian News Agency]] | archive-date=3 April 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160403221734/http://www.usubc.org/AUR/aur706.php#a17 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Political life==
On 30 March 1990, Yukhnovskyi was elected with 59.07% votes (out of 6 candidates) as a member of [[Verkhovna Rada|parliament]] of [[Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic|Ukrainian SSR]] from an election district in the city of [[Lviv]].  On 15 May 1990, he became the leader of the first ever opposition party in the [[Verkhovna Rada|Ukrainian SSR parliament]] named [[Democratic Bloc (Ukraine)|Narodna Rada]] (''People’s Council''). Yukhnovskyi was one of the co-authors of the [[Declaration of State Sovereignty of Ukraine]].<ref name=ist/>

During the 24 August 1991 parliamentary debate preceding the [[Declaration of Independence of Ukraine]] Yukhnovskyi was the MP who first called on parliament to immediately declare Ukraine an independent democratic state.<ref>[https://ukrainianweek.com/History/222470 A reform that ruined the Soviet Union], [[The Ukrainian Week]] (10 November 2018)</ref>

In the [[1991 Ukrainian presidential election|first presidential elections in Ukraine]] Yukhnovskyi was supported by 554,719 voters (1.74%) and took 5th place out of 6 candidates. In 1992 he was appointed the first vice [[Prime Minister of Ukraine]].

In the [[1994 Ukrainian parliamentary election|1994 parliamentary elections]] Yukhnovskyi was elected to the parliament in the same electoral district as in 1990, the city of Lviv, with 60.41% of support. In the [[1998 Ukrainian parliamentary election|1998 parliamentary elections]] he was elected as #15 in the [[People's Movement of Ukraine]] (Rukh) party list. In the [[2002 Ukrainian parliamentary election|2002 parliamentary elections]] he was again elected as #68 now in the [[Our Ukraine–People's Self-Defense Bloc|Our Ukraine]] party list.<ref name="Verkhovna Rada"/>

Yukhnovsky was an author of over 400 scientific papers, five books and a textbook "Osnovy kvantovoyi mekhaniky" (''Fundamentals of [[Quantum Mechanics]]''). As a member of the parliament he actively participated in passing of over 100 bills. He was one of the authors of the [[Act of Declaration of Independence of Ukraine]].

Ihor Yukhnovskyi was the head of [[All-Ukrainian Union of World War II veterans]]. He supported the reconciliation of veterans of the [[Soviet Army]] and the [[Ukrainian Insurgent Army]].

In 2006, Ukrainian President [[Viktor Yushchenko]] appointed Ihor Yukhnovskyi director of the [[Ukrainian Institute of National Memory]].<ref name=USUBC/>

Yukhnovskyi died in Lviv on 26 March 2024, at the age of 98.<ref>{{cite news |title=Помер фізик-теоретик і Герой України Ігор Юхновський |url=https://suspilne.media/714150-pomer-fizik-teoretik-i-geroj-ukraini-igor-uhnovskij/ |access-date=26 March 2024 |publisher=Suspilne Media |date=26 March 2024}}</ref><ref name=ist/>

==Commemoration and legacy==
On Yukhnovskyi's 101st birthday in 2026, one of the streets of [[Lviv]] was renamed in his honour, and a [[garden square|square]] with a memorial [[stele]] dedicated to the academician was unveiled in presence of the city's mayor [[Andriy Sadovyi]], Yukhnovsyki's daughter Natalia Hurska and human rights activist [[Myroslav Marynovych]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=У Львові відкрили вулицю Ігоря Юхновського та оновили сквер|date=2026-09-01|url=https://zaxid.net/u_lvovi_vidkrili_vulitsyu_igorya_yuhnovskogo_ta_onovili_skver_n1644808|access-date=2026-09-01}}</ref><ref name=ist>{{Cite web|title=У Львові відкрили вулицю на честь академіка Ігоря Юхновського|date=2026-09-01|url=https://www.istpravda.com.ua/short/2026/09/1/166132/|access-date=2026-09-01}}</ref>
